title: Swipeboard: compact GPU briefing + burst controls
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Mobile-first compact briefing card and swipeboard for Dedicated GPU pools. Goal: give operators a focused, single-row briefing that surfaces pool health, hot path latency, current autoscale policy, burst budget, and a minimal set of immediate controls (pause/force-burst/quick-override) without opening the full pool detail panel. This ticket covers the UI concepts, low-fidelity prototypes, accessibility review, and handoff artifacts for ENG to implement the compact briefing as a reusable console component.
acceptance_criteria: Compact swipeboard renders at pool list level and as a pinned strip in Pool Overview
Displays real-time health sparkline, 1m/5m/1h token throughput, and current preflight SLO breach risk indicator
Burst budget slider exposes minutes remaining and predicted cost delta; changing slider generates a preview action modal and is gated by confirmation
Autoscale policy summary shows hysteresis windows, min/max nodes, and predicted scale direction based on current trend
Accessible: keyboard focus order, ARIA labels for controls, color contrast meets AA
Prototype links, spec doc, and component tokens are in Figma and Confluence for ENG handoff
engineering_notes: Backend should surface precomputed 'burst_budget_seconds' and 'predicted_cost_delta' to avoid heavy client computation
Prefer incremental websocket updates for sparkline + throughput; degrade gracefully to 30s polling in private deployments
Control actions (force-burst/pause) must call feature-flagged endpoint 'v1/pools/:id/brief-actions' and support optimistic UI with rollback on error
Telemetry: emit user interaction events for every quick-override and cost-preview confirmation
review_feedback: PM (Liam O'Neill): prioritize cost-preview clarity; show delta both as % and absolute USD estimate
Eng (Miguel Ortega): request we avoid embedding complex prediction models in client; prefer server-side predictions and short TTL caching
Security (Priya Kapoor): confirm RBAC mapping for quick controls (only admins and pool-ops role can force-burst)
Design (Evelyn Martinez): adjust color mapping for 'risk' indicator to use pattern + color for colorblind accessibility
decisions: Use compact horizontal layout with three progressive reveal states: collapsed, brief, expanded - to reduce noise in pool list
Burst slider shows time budget rather than percentage; agreed with finance to surface cost delta in both short and long horizons
Use a confirm modal for any disruptive action that changes autoscale policy or consumes burst budget
Expose a small inline 'why' tooltip linked to console Help center for every non-obvious metric (KV cache hit rate, SLO risk)
tradeoffs: Compact mode reduces cognitive load but hides detailed node-level telemetry; added quick-expand affordance to jump to full pool view
Real-time websocket updates increase server load for large fleets; decided to only open websockets for pools visible on the viewport (lazy connect)
Cost preview accuracy vs latency: prioritized modestly-smoothed server-side predictions (10s TTL) over exact, slower batch recompute
next_steps: Address engineering clarifications in PRD and schedule 1:1 with infra to confirm websocket scaling (owner: Miguel Ortega)
Prepare final high-fidelity frames for accessibility pass (owner: Sofia Chen) by 2025-03-07
Create feature flag scaffold (feature: compact-swipeboard) and add rollout plan to console-2025.03 release notes
Sync with Finance to finalize USD cost conversion assumptions and thresholds for 'high cost' badge
